page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the ecs.sn1ne family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance features 16 dedicated physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, providing a total of 16 vCPUs. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Virtualization is managed via the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core workloads. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression also show poor throughput. Conversely, multi-core performance is average, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth remains average across both small and large block read/write tests, though the Passmark memory score is weak.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average multi-core performance, the ecs.sn1ne.4xlarge is suited for compute-heavy workloads that can leverage parallel processing but do not require high memory density or local storage. Suitable workloads include multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, static web serving, and database operations. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable multi-core performance, though the older Intel Xeon architecture represents a tradeoff compared to newer hardware generations.
